Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m first loading the workspace contract, then I’ll use the required fish-control bookshelf and visual-evidence skill before touching the policy. I’ll trace the assigned parent and sampled rollout evidence, make one bounded controller change, and update both the notes and reusable guidance before validating the candidate.

The inherited guidance says this lineage is already well beyond the naive seed: the durable mechanism is LOS-rate C-bend control plus persistent same-side posterior phase recruitment, while instantaneous moment allocation and noncausal recoil fitting have failed. I’m now checking the four same-generation rollouts—including both visual rows—to determine whether this candidate should preserve the replicated route and introduce a genuinely new, bounded mechanism.

The visual/metric comparison is decisive: the three exact-parent repeats and the helpful-moment variant all self-propel with the same coherent alternating wake and all capture in `18.656–18.733T`; the variant’s `0.0165T` edge is smaller than known same-policy spread. No sampled failure exists in this quartet, so I’m treating the inherited `22.011T` recoil-observer rollout as the informative control failure and not inventing a visual failure. The bookshelf consultation is now mandatory under the user’s protocol because several completed iterations changed allocation details without a durable semantic gain.

The selected mechanism is a near-target closing-speed envelope, not another steering gain or moment residual. It will leave the replicated LOS/C-bend/phase route untouched and only contract the anterior oscillator’s limit-cycle amplitude smoothly when three observed conditions coincide: normalized range is near, radial closing speed is already high, and the target remains ahead in the body frame. The evidence sets the activation regime (`~2.7L` at `16T`, `~0.72–0.75U` closing through capture); the bookshelf contributes only the invariant that sensor feedback may modulate a productive CPG envelope without replacing route control.

The policy, candidate notes, and reusable guidance are now all materially updated. The controller change is deliberately isolated: the new range/closing-speed gate affects only the Van der Pol amplitude term; the LOS route, posterior traveling-wave coefficients, steering centers, phase actuator, and feasibility projection are byte-for-byte unchanged. I’m moving through schema, syntax, reflection/safety, and workspace-contract checks now—no CFD will be run.

A custom no-CFD reflection/gate test hit an environment issue before executing: `julia` is not on this shell’s `PATH`. I’m checking the workspace/toolchain locations now; if the runtime truly is absent, I’ll still complete every Python/static contract check and report that exact verification limitation rather than treating it as a policy failure.

An offline replay of the new gate against all three exact-parent traces confirms it is genuinely terminal and bounded: it first exceeds 1% relief around `15.65–15.68T` at roughly `2.92–2.94L`, peaks at only `16.3–16.9%`, and leaves the early wake-building route effectively unchanged. This is not a surrogate outcome claim; it only verifies that the proposed observation/actuator translation matches the intended evidence window.

Final contract status is stable: the required guidance semantic check passes, the solver boundary check passes, and the static schema/scope audit finds all 32 `params.*` references backed by returned fields. The mandated lightweight Julia assertion remains unexecutable solely because this environment has no `julia` binary; the check runner confirmed it never reached candidate loading. No CFD was run.

Produced exactly one candidate: a bounded closing-speed carrier envelope that preserves all existing steering/phase authority while reducing late anterior oscillation amplitude by at most 20%.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

Validation passed for guidance semantics, parameter schema/scope, required artifacts, and solver boundaries. The Julia contract test could not execute because `julia` is absent from the environment; the check runner confirmed this was the sole failure. No CFD was run.
